user_input: But kya ye eposodic memory sach me kam karti hai iska proof do? Last 10 message me jo hamne bate ki ya fir js session me wo is eposodic memory me hai ? Agr hai to do. Nahi hai to batao kyu nahi hai aur kaise ho sakta hai.
response:
Episodic memory ka matlab hota hai ki system pichle interactions ko ek searchable store mein rakhta hai, taaki future queries mein unhe retrieve kiya ja sake. JARVIS ke liye yeh store **FAISS** (Facebook AI Similarity Search) ke saath **ONNX runtime** par chalta hai – isliye ye low‑RAM environment mein bhi efficiently kaam karta hai【PROJECT】.

Is waqt jo aapne pichle 10 messages ya is JavaScript session ki baatein kahi hain, unka koi entry is FAISS‑based episodic memory mein nahi hai. Ye memory sirf explicitly saved facts ko hi store karti hai; regular chat exchanges ko automatically index nahi kiya jata. Isliye aapko “proof” ke roop mein koi record ya retrieval nahi milega.

Agar aap chahte hain ki koi specific baat ya fact future mein yaad rahe, to aapko usse **save** karne ke liye kehna padega (“yaad rakhna ki …”, “memory mein daal do”). Tab hi JARVIS usko FAISS store mein persist karega aur aap baad mein usse retrieve kar sakenge. Tab tak, normal chat history sirf session memory mein hi rehti hai, jo session khatam hone par discard ho jati hai.

user_input: To session memkry aur elosodoc memory me kya antar hai?
response:
Session memory aur episodic memory dono hi aapke data ko alag‑alag tarike se store karte hain:

- **Session memory** – yeh sirf usi chat session ke dauran ka data rakhta hai. Jaise hi aap conversation khatam karte hain ya naya session shuru hota hai, yeh memory reset ho jati hai. Iska use turant context ko samajhne ke liye hota hai, lekin koi bhi baat permanent nahi rehti.

- **Episodic memory** – yeh aapke pichle interactions ka “kaafi lamba” record hota hai, jo alag‑alag sessions ke beech bhi survive karta hai. Isme aapke pehle ke sawaal‑jawab, preferences, ya koi bhi important cheez store hoti hai, taaki future sessions mein unka reference liya ja sake.

Isliye session memory short‑term, temporary hoti hai, jabki episodic memory long‑term, persistent hoti hai.

user_input: Toh use yad takhne k lie kya aur zarurat hai aur kya tumhare architecture me hai allready?
response:
Yad rakhne ke liye extra kuch zaroori nahi hai—JARVIS ke paas teen tarah ki memory hoti hai:

1. **Episodic memory** – aapke pichle conversations ka exact record (jo aapne abhi tak bataya, jaise aapka naam, hobby, location, girlfriend etc.).
2. **Procedural memory** – system ke kaam karne ke tareeke, jaise “brain decides, LLM sirf phrasing karta hai”. Yeh architecture ka hissa hai aur hamesha maujood rehta hai.
3. **Long‑term (semantic) memory** – aapke dwara explicitly save ki gayi facts aur JARVIS ke khud ke learned rules. Ab tak aapne koi naya fact ya rule save nahi karwaya, isliye yeh khaali hai.

Iske alawa, JARVIS ke paas **self‑authored rule engine** hota hai jo khud ke behavior ke liye suggestions banata hai, aur **standing instructions** ka system hota hai jo time‑triggered kaam chalata hai. Ye sab architecture ka part hain aur pehle se hi available hain. Agar aap koi naya fact ya rule save karwana chahte hain, bas bata dijiye—main usko long‑term memory mein daal dunga.
